title: Booker T. Washington's successor Robert Moton and growing up with his children
summary: Washington was dead before Wilson arrived; he discusses Principal Moton, the Moton children, and the quality of Tuskegee education.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Uh huh. Did you ever get to know Booker T. Washington to see him or ...
No, by the time my mother and my brother and I had joined my father at Tuskegee, Booker T. Washington had died, and Robert Moten was the new principal.
So he was the principal while I was there at Tuskegee.
Did you ever hear your mother discuss with either your dad or you any impressions of Mr. Moten, as to what he was like?
No, Mr. Moten, who took his place.

Oh, Well, I knew Mr. Moten, and he had children of the same age as me and my brother. So we grew up with Moten kids, the younger Moten children -- there were two older and two younger than me and my brother.

One became a drummer, a musician, and so we were in close contact with those children, but not the Booker T. family. My father was a great admirer of Booker T. -- I think that was one reason he took that job.

He thought Booker T. was a very outstanding man at that time. And you have to remember that Booker T. Washington was born a slave and finally founding a school that is, to this day, one of the leading black colleges of the south.

Of course, times have changed now, you know, since the Supreme Court ordered desegregation of the schools, all of those segregated colleges are in a different position from what they were in those days. But they surely furnished a tremendous -- they filled a tremendous gap in the South. There was Tuskegee, Moorhouse, Atlanta University, and there comes to mind so many of those schools, those segregated schools.
But I do think that Tuskegee, back in those days in the twenties, we were getting education comparable to the northern schools of today in 1979 in a lot of ways.
